posts.title: Capitals collapse in final minutes leads to tough-to-take loss against Panthers: numbers for the morning after
posts.description: The Washington Capitals really know how to lose a hockey game this season. Friday night’s defeat to the Florida Panthers was especially cruel, though, as the team allowed two late goals, going from in control to completely out of time. After it was all said and done, the Capitals left with zero standings points in a 3-2 loss . Brutal stuff. View this post on Instagram I really loved what I saw from the Capitals in the first period, but then they lost that edge and let the Panthers dictate the pace and tempo for the rest of regulation. That shift was painfully obvious analytically, as after recording 5 five-on-five high-danger chances in the first 20 minutes, the Caps didn’t create a single one in the remaining 40 minutes. It’s going to take some heroics to win a game playing like that, and they almost got them from their rookie defender. posts.title: Alex Ovechkin’s diminishing role reaches new extreme after receiving career-low 7:50 of ice time against Panthers
posts.description: Alex Ovechkin received the lowest ice time of his career (in a game where he didn’t suffer an injury or get ejected) in the Washington Capitals ’ 3-2 loss to the Florida Panthers on Friday. Taking the ice on a line with Dylan Strome and Anthony Beauvillier , the 41-year-old forward played just 7:50, with 3:31 in the first period, 2:12 in the second, and 2:07 in the third. Notably, Ovechkin took the ice for just 33 seconds on the power play. He has no PPGs and just one power-play point this season. While Ovechkin didn’t see the ice much, his line-mates both got into double digits, with Strome getting 13:42 TOI and Beauvillier getting 10:40. Ovechkin was the only Capitals player not to see more than 10 minutes. Ovechkin’s 7:50 of ice time against the Panthers is 3:06 less than his previous career low — 10:56 in a game against the Nashville Predators on October 29. posts.title: Matvei Michkov scratched by Flyers after another ‘intense’ altercation with teammate, reportedly Porter Martone
posts.description: The next chapter of drama involving Matvei Michkov and the Philadelphia Flyers has been written. Philadelphia made headlines for their cryptic scratching of Michkov against the Vancouver Canucks on Friday for a “violation of team rules,” and we now know what that violation was. According to Sportsnet’s Frank Seravalli , Michkov got into another altercation with a teammate earlier this week during the Flyers’ 7-3 loss to the Washington Capitals . Unlike some of Michkov’s other flare-ups, cameras didn’t catch the offense this time, but Seravalli reports the team felt Michkov was “clearly the aggressor,” and the war of words spilled into the locker room. Seravalli added that it is unclear whether the altercation turned physical, but multiple sources called the scene “intense.” Daily Faceoff’s Anthony Di Marco added that he has heard from sources that the player Michkov got “involved with” this time was fellow young winger Porter Martone .
